threads.body: [Testing] Remove `@Nullable` here; this repository's Java test rules prohibit adding nullability annotations to test code.

replies.body: Removed the `@Nullable` annotation (and its import) from the test.

threads.body: [General] This recursive descent has no nesting limit, so a sufficiently deep but valid JSON body throws `StackOverflowError`. The handler in `sanitize` catches only `RuntimeException`; in the javaagent path the outer advice suppresses the error and skips span creation instead of merely omitting the query attribute. Please use iterative traversal or reject input at an explicit safe depth before recursing.

replies.body:
Fixed by bounding the recursion depth. `maskObject` and `maskArray` now call `enterNesting()`, which increments a `depth` counter and throws `NestingTooDeepException` once it exceeds `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` (200); every non-throwing return decrements. `NestingTooDeepException` extends `RuntimeException`, so the existing handler in `sanitize` catches it and drops the body (attribute omitted, never captured raw), matching the fail-safe already used for malformed input.

I kept the recursive descent rather than rewriting to an iterative traversal: a depth cap is a few lines and obviously correct, whereas an explicit stack rewrite would be a much larger diff. The cap is chosen on its own terms — the walker uses roughly two frames per nesting level and runs on the application's own thread, which may have a small stack, and real Elasticsearch bodies nest at most a few dozen levels, so 200 sits well above any realistic query while staying safe on a small stack. Added a test that nests past the cap and asserts the attribute is omitted.

threads.body: [Naming] This exception is intentionally unused, so name it `ignored` per the repository's catch-variable convention (`.github/copilot-instructions.md:28-36`).

replies.body: Renamed the catch variable to `ignored`. It remains unused after the depth-cap change, so the convention applies.

threads.body: [General] This drops every `_msearch` and `_msearch/template` query when sanitization is enabled. Those endpoints are marked as search endpoints (`ElasticsearchEndpointMap.java:253,397`), but their valid request format is an NDJSON sequence of header/body objects; `readBody()` concatenates those lines, so after the first object this branch always sees trailing content and returns `null`. Please sanitize the complete NDJSON sequence (without ever falling back to raw text) and cover both multi-search endpoints.

replies.body:
Addressed in 7c4b5bf3095b1f4e508cb56c2e7229fda7163dd5.

Analysis: The comment is valid. `readBody()` removes NDJSON line separators, which leaves adjacent top-level header and body objects. The sanitizer now scans every top-level JSON value and inserts the same semicolon separator used by the OpenSearch instrumentation. It still returns null if any value is malformed or exceeds the nesting limit. Parameterized getter coverage exercises both `msearch` and `msearch_template`.

Upsides: Sanitized query capture now works for both multi-search endpoints. Every scalar in every NDJSON object remains masked, and malformed sequences are still dropped without a raw-text fallback.

Downsides: The sanitizer now accepts multiple top-level JSON values for any search endpoint, not only multi-search endpoints. This does not expose raw data because every accepted value is fully masked.

threads.body: [General] Valid low-level REST endpoints do not have to start with `/`—this module already calls `new Request("GET", "_cluster/health")` successfully. With v3-preview, an equivalent `new Request("POST", "_search")` reaches this branch with no endpoint definition and is rejected, so its query is never captured. Normalize an optional leading slash instead of requiring one.

replies.body:
Addressed in 1c1def292ad034b22076f52b8c7d938299fb5e24.

Analysis: The fallback endpoint matcher required a leading slash even though the Elasticsearch REST clients accept endpoints without one. It now strips a leading slash only when present and applies the same segment validation to both forms.

Upsides: V3-preview captures and sanitizes search bodies for valid slashless endpoints. Tests cover slashless paths with one, two, and three segments.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] Enabling capture here does not implement the advertised v3-preview behavior for the REST 5.0 and 6.4 javaagents. Both instrumentations still call `ElasticsearchRestRequest.create(method, endpoint)` without the request entity, so `getDbQueryText()` always sees `httpEntity == null`; only the 7.0 advice passes the body. Please propagate the entity in the 5.0/6.4 advice paths and cover their v3-preview capture behavior.

replies.body:
Addressed in 2ec2ef59d3e6a060159d1a5fc08e7461c87272b9.

Analysis: The REST 5.0 advice receives the entity as its fourth argument, and the REST 6.4 Request exposes it through getEntity(). Both advice paths now pass that entity to ElasticsearchRestRequest so the shared attribute getter can sanitize and capture search bodies.

Upsides: The REST 5.0 and 6.4 javaagents now implement the advertised v3-preview behavior. Integration tests verify that each version captures a sanitized query only under v3-preview.

Downsides: The two new v3-preview Testcontainers tasks add CI runtime for these modules.

threads.body: [General] This rejects the legacy typed search route `/{index}/{type}/_search`, even though it is valid in the REST 5.0 and 6.4 versions that share this getter. Those low-level-client requests have no endpoint definition, so under v3-preview their bodies are never captured. Recognize the typed route here and move `/test-index/_doc/_search` from the rejection cases to the accepted cases.

replies.body:
Addressed in f8e866f81b6c3f26dc66f0227f8aedd96be652ad.

Analysis: Elasticsearch REST 5.0 and 6.4 accept three-segment typed search routes. The fallback matcher now treats a three-segment path ending in `_search` as a search endpoint.

Upsides: V3-preview captures and sanitizes low-level typed search bodies for the client versions that support this route. Tests cover both leading-slash forms.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] `AgentListener.afterAgent()` is not guaranteed to finish before application instrumentation runs. On Java 8 with a custom JUL manager, `AgentInstaller` deliberately delays these callbacks until `LogManager` loads and then runs them on a new daemon thread (`javaagent-tooling/.../AgentInstaller.java:368-401,520-537`). The first Elasticsearch request can therefore race this registration; `ElasticsearchQuerySanitizerAccess.sanitize()` still sees `null` and silently drops the query even though v3-preview promises capture. Register the bridge from an eager agent-installation hook (for example, while loading the Elasticsearch `InstrumentationModule`) rather than from `afterAgent()`.

replies.body: I think we can ignore this for now.

threads.body: [General] `BufferedReader.lines()` wraps an I/O failure encountered while consuming the stream in `UncheckedIOException`, so this `IOException` handler does not catch mid-read failures. With v3-preview the library instrumentation now enters this path by default, and `RestClientWrapper` does not suppress exceptions from `instrumenter.start()`, allowing telemetry extraction to abort the Elasticsearch request. Catch `UncheckedIOException` as well and drop the body as intended.
